record.scope: The two units in appliesTo declare MIMIC: Mime Jr. (1 star) and Mr. Mime (2 stars); both maxPP 80, range 2, no passive. MIMIC has no numbers of its own: what it does depends entirely on the ability of its current target, so this record describes the dispatch rule, not any copied ability's effect.

dispatch.registry: AbilityStrategies[Ability.MIMIC] = new MimicStrategy() (class defined in abilities.ts, line 688)
dispatch.strategy: MimicStrategy extends AbilityStrategy; at runtime it forwards to AbilityStrategies[target.skill]

record.summary: MIMIC casts a copy of its target's ability. The cast is made on the unit's current attack target (an enemy). If the target's current skill is not in InimitableAbilities, MimicStrategy.process calls AbilityStrategies[target.skill].process(caster, board, target, crit) directly, so the copied ability runs with the caster as the user (the caster's stars, AP, items, position and range; the crit flag rolled for the MIMIC cast) and with that same target; the PP spend and animation come from the copied strategy's own super.process (not from MimicStrategy). If the target's skill is inimitable (the list includes MIMIC, METRONOME, SKETCH, SKILL_SWAP, ASSIST, ENCORE, all HIDDEN_POWER_*, and others) only the base process runs: PP is spent and the ability is broadcast, with no effect. The caster's own skill is not changed by the cast.

targeting.who: the unit's current attack target (single enemy); the copied ability then applies its own targeting with that target
targeting.note: MIMIC keeps the default requiresTarget = true; the copied strategy's own requiresTarget is not consulted (the cast has already been gated by MIMIC's flag and the target was passed in). A copied ability that expects a null target (requiresTarget false) receives the enemy target instead; what that does was not traced per ability.

geometry.shape: depends on the copied ability; none for MIMIC itself

declaredRaw.copiedFrom: target.skill at the moment of the cast
declaredRaw.rule: copy unless target.skill is in InimitableAbilities

effects.scaling: none of its own. Amounts, ranges and star tables are those of the copied strategy, indexed by the CASTER's stars (pokemon.stars), with the caster's AP, stats and items.
effects.resolution: AbilityStrategies[target.skill].process(pokemon, board, target, crit): runs the copied strategy's process; its own super.process spends PP (maxPP of the caster) and broadcasts. The crit flag is the one rolled for the MIMIC cast by castAbility (ABILITY_CRIT on the caster; MIMIC's canCritByDefault is false). Copied abilities that read canCritByDefault do so only through castAbility, which is not re-entered.
super.process only: pp = max(0, pp - maxPP), ult count incremented, ability broadcast; nothing else.

starBehavior.note: MIMIC has no star table. The caster's star count only matters inside the copied strategy's own tables.

record.positionalConditions: None for MIMIC itself. The copied ability's own conditions apply, evaluated from the caster's position and the passed target.
record.repeatedCastsAndModes: No stored state: every cast re-reads target.skill. The skill is whatever the target currently holds, which another effect (e.g. SKILL_SWAP) could have changed during the fight; not traced.
record.rawVsResolved: No declared numbers. Requested/applied amounts belong to the copied ability; they are resolved with the caster's stars and AP. The effect of one MIMIC cast on a given enemy is therefore the record of that enemy's ability evaluated with Mime Jr. / Mr. Mime as the caster.
